note: SmartESS M9 engineering knowledge base. Every document marked VERIFIED was downloaded from the official publisher/manufacturer/repository host, opened with the project PDF tooling, and had its identity corroborated by the text of the PDF itself (title page, document number, revision, author list), never by a search-result snippet alone. mechanisms/observables/test_conditions are declared only where the extracted document text actually discusses the item; they are never inferred from a title. Documents that could not be legitimately obtained are marked NEEDS_MANUAL_ACCESS, need OCR, were rejected, or remain unresolved - they declare no coverage. Access controls were never bypassed, no paywall was circumvented, and nothing was fabricated.

documents.title: ECPE Guideline AQG 324 - Qualification of Power Modules for Use in Power Electronics Converter Units in Motor Vehicles (incl. SiC Annex), Release 04.1/2025
documents.publisher: ECPE European Center for Power Electronics e.V.
documents.citation: ECPE European Center for Power Electronics e.V. (Working Group 'Automotive Power Module Qualification'), "ECPE Guideline AQG 324: Qualification of Power Modules for Use in Power Electronics Converter Units in Motor Vehicles," Release 04.1/2025, released 31.03.2025. https://www.ecpe.org/research/working-groups/automotive-aqg-324/
documents.description: ECPE's public automotive power-module qualification guideline (145 pages, including the SiC annex). Defines module, characterising, environmental and lifetime test programmes: two power-cycling procedures (PCsec, PCmin), thermal shock, HTRB, HTGB, H3TRB, dynamic gate and reverse-bias stress, plus determination of thermal resistance (Rth). Discusses chip-near and chip-remote interconnection (wire/ribbon bond, Cu clip, sintering, soldering) and die-attach technologies, and specifies measurement of gate-source threshold voltage, gate leakage and drain-source reverse leakage as module-test parameters. It specifies test procedures and requirements; it does not prescribe a one-to-one mapping from any measured parameter to a physical failure mechanism.

documents.title: High-performance SiC MOSFET technology for power electronics design
documents.citation: P. Friedrichs (Infineon Technologies AG), "High-performance SiC MOSFET technology for power electronics design," Infineon article v01_00-EN, November 2019. https://www.infineon.com/dgdl/Infineon-High-performance_SiC_MOSFET_technology_for_power_electronics_design-Article-v01_00-EN.pdf
documents.description: Manufacturer technology article (10 pages). Reviews SiC MOSFET device design and the 4H-SiC/SiO2 gate-oxide system, on-state resistance behaviour, threshold voltage, and the trade-offs that SiC device engineering has to manage. Discusses gate-oxide reliability and threshold-voltage considerations as design concerns rather than as diagnosis rules. The PDF's own metadata corroborates the title and identifies Infineon as the authoring source, and the body names Peter Friedrichs.

documents.title: Guidelines for CoolSiC MOSFET gate drive voltage window
documents.citation: Infineon Technologies AG, "Guidelines for CoolSiC MOSFET gate drive voltage window," Application Note AN2018-09, retrieved revision dated 2025-05-26.
documents.description: Infineon application note AN2018-09 (20 pages). Explains the recommended gate-drive voltage window and the long-term behaviour of the gate threshold voltage under switching operation, including how the applied gate bias level relates to threshold-voltage stability and to on-state resistance/temperature behaviour. It discusses gate-bias operating conditions and threshold-voltage drift as a device-behaviour topic; it does not assert that a threshold-voltage shift identifies a specific failure mode.

documents.title: Understanding and interpreting the CoolSiC MOSFET 1200 V datasheet
documents.citation: Infineon Technologies AG, "Understanding and interpreting the CoolSiC MOSFET 1200 V datasheet," Application Note AN2025-10, V 1.1, 2026-07-15.
documents.description: Infineon application note AN2025-10 (32 pages, V 1.1). The candidate was recorded as an amorphous 'CoolSiC 1200 V application-note collection'; this entry is the single canonical note actually selected. It explains how datasheet parameters for 1200 V CoolSiC MOSFETs are defined and measured - on-state resistance, threshold voltage, gate and drain leakage, thermal resistance and junction/case temperatures - and how to apply them in system design. It documents measurement conventions and parameter meaning, not failure attribution.

documents.title: Designed to Last, Even in the Harshest Environments
documents.citation: G. Moxey and D. Gajewski, "Designed to Last, Even in the Harshest Environments: A ground-up strategy to enable better system durability in tough operating conditions," Wolfspeed whitepaper, 4 November 2025.
documents.description: Wolfspeed reliability whitepaper (12 pages) built around the reliability bathtub curve. Enumerates early-life, useful-life and wear-out failure candidates for SiC MOSFETs and modules, including gate-oxide wear-out and threshold-voltage instability, and reports qualification-style stress results (high-temperature reverse bias, high humidity H3TRB, temperature cycling and power cycling) with their applied conditions. It presents mechanisms as candidates and reports measured parameter behaviour rather than asserting one observable identifies one mechanism.

documents.title: SiC Power Module Reliability: Wolfspeed's Power Cycling and Lifetime Modeling Approach
documents.citation: M. Ceresa and R. Shaw, "SiC Power Module Reliability: Wolfspeed's Power Cycling and Lifetime Modeling Approach," Wolfspeed whitepaper, 12 November 2025.
documents.description: Wolfspeed whitepaper (11 pages) on power cycling and lifetime modelling for SiC power modules. Covers the fundamentals of power cycling, contrasts silicon and SiC failure candidates (including die-attach/solder and bond-wire fatigue and the role of thermal resistance and junction temperature), describes testing methodology and measurement, and builds life models. Thermal resistance and junction temperature appear as monitored quantities and inputs to lifetime models; the document does not reduce package degradation to a single electrical observable.

documents.title: Mitigating Package Induced Failures
documents.citation: Wolfspeed, Inc., "Mitigating Package Induced Failures," Application Note PRD-09129, Rev. 1, May 2025.
documents.description: Wolfspeed application note PRD-09129 Rev. 1 (16 pages). Systematically walks the power-module construction - baseplate, substrate (DBC/DAB/IMS), die-to-substrate attach (solder/sinter), die, interconnects (wire bonds, leads, clips) and encapsulation - and then discusses chip-level and package-level failure candidates and their limitations, including wire-bond and die-attach limitations and a structured root-cause ('5 Whys') approach. It is a package-reliability reference that treats package failure mechanisms as a family of candidates to be distinguished, not as a single-cause diagnosis.

documents.title: Mounting Recommendations and Thermal Measurement for Wolfspeed SiC Power Devices in Through-Hole Packages
documents.citation: Wolfspeed, Inc., "Mounting Recommendations and Thermal Measurement for Wolfspeed SiC Power Devices in Through-Hole Packages," Application Note PRD-05652.
documents.description: The canonical PDF was obtained from Wolfspeed's asset host (23 pages) and its identity is corroborated by Wolfspeed's own product-page listing of PRD-05652 under that exact title. However the file has no text layer: text extraction across all 23 pages yields 33 characters in total (a few digits from one table). No OCR path exists in SmartESS, so this document is NOT ingested and no mechanisms, observables or test conditions are declared for it. documents.title: Impact of VGS on SiC MOSFET Characteristics
documents.citation: Wolfspeed, Inc., "Impact of VGS on SiC MOSFET Characteristics," Application Note PRD-08937, Rev. 1, November 2024.
documents.description: Wolfspeed application note PRD-08937 Rev. 1 (13 pages). Quantifies how the applied gate-source voltage (VGS) changes SiC MOSFET characteristics: current capability, on-state resistance at 25 C and 175 C, turn-on/off waveforms and switching losses. On-state resistance is shown to depend strongly on gate voltage and temperature, which is direct evidence that RDS(on) alone cannot isolate a degradation mechanism. It characterises gate-voltage dependence of device behaviour; it makes no failure-diagnosis claim.

documents.title: Sintering Considerations and the Die Top System
documents.citation: Wolfspeed, Inc., "Sintering Considerations and the Die Top System," Application Note PRD-07969, Rev. 3, April 2024.
documents.description: Manufacturer-expansion source added to fill the die-attach coverage gap. Wolfspeed application note PRD-07969 Rev. 3 (22 pages) specifies sinter paste printing, drying, pick-and-place, the sinter process and die-top-system processing, front/backside metallisation, die layout and wire-bonding implications, plus quality assurance. It is the corpus's most explicit die-attach/thermal-path/interconnection construction reference, describing the physical interfaces whose degradation is studied elsewhere in the corpus. It specifies process and construction, not diagnostics.

documents.title: Enhancing System Durability with Advanced Packaging for Silicon Carbide (SiC)
documents.citation: A. Barkley, "Enhancing System Durability with Advanced Packaging for Silicon Carbide (SiC)," Wolfspeed whitepaper, 4 November 2025.
documents.description: Manufacturer-expansion source (Wolfspeed whitepaper, 8 pages) on advanced SiC packaging for durability and power density. Discusses package architectures, die attach and sintering, thermal path and thermal resistance, and how packaging choices determine the thermo-mechanical stresses that drive wear-out, in the context of power-cycling and temperature-cycling duty. It frames packaging as a durability strategy rather than defining diagnostic criteria.

documents.title: SiC Power Devices and Modules - Application Note
documents.citation: ROHM Co., Ltd., "SiC Power Devices and Modules," Application Note, Rev.001, June 2013 (13103EAY01).
documents.description: Manufacturer-expansion source added for manufacturer diversity (ROHM). The official ROHM SiC application note (41 pages, Rev.001, June 2013) covers SiC material and device characteristics, SiC MOSFET and Schottky diode behaviour, gate drive and on-resistance behaviour, and a reliability section that describes SiC-MOSFET reliability testing including high-temperature gate-bias and high-temperature reverse-bias style stresses and gate-oxide reliability discussion. It is an older revision (2013) and should be weighted accordingly; it is recorded here because it is the manufacturer's own reliability reference and no superseding public revision was located. Its reliability content is broad and descriptive.

documents.title: Driving MB and MC Family mSiC MOSFETs
documents.citation: Microchip Technology Inc., "Driving MB and MC Family mSiC MOSFETs," Application Note AN6239, DS00006239A, 2025.
documents.description: Manufacturer-expansion source added for manufacturer diversity (Microchip). Application note AN6239 (14 pages) gives guidance on selecting gate drive voltages for mSiC MOSFET families and discusses how gate drive voltage selection affects device performance, on-state resistance, threshold voltage, switching behaviour, efficiency and reliability, including the gate-stress implications of the recommended drive window. It is a gate-drive guidance document; it does not define diagnostic rules.

documents.title: 1.2 kV-Class SiC MOSFET Equipped with Embedded SBD for Improvement of Reliability
documents.citation: Toshiba Electronic Devices & Storage Corporation, "1.2 kV-Class SiC MOSFET Equipped with Embedded SBD for Improvement of Reliability," Toshiba Technical Review.
documents.description: Manufacturer-expansion source added for manufacturer diversity (Toshiba). Technical-review article (5 pages) on a 1.2 kV SiC MOSFET with an embedded Schottky barrier diode. It motivates the design by SiC reliability concerns - in particular gate-oxide reliability and the body-diode/bipolar-degradation effects that shift on-resistance - and reports on-resistance and threshold-voltage behaviour. It is a device-design reliability paper from a manufacturer and discusses mechanism candidates rather than diagnostics.

documents.title: Failure Characterization of Discrete SiC MOSFETs under Forward Power Cycling Test
documents.citation: T. Huang, B. P. Singh, Y. Liu and S. Norrga, "Failure Characterization of Discrete SiC MOSFETs under Forward Power Cycling Test," Energies, vol. 17, no. 11, art. 2557, 2024. doi:10.3390/en17112557
documents.description: Open-access primary research (Energies 17(11):2557, 23 pages). Performs forward power cycling on discrete SiC MOSFETs and characterises the resulting degradation across electrical and thermal parameters - on-state resistance, threshold voltage, gate and drain leakage, on-state voltage, thermal resistance and junction/case temperatures - while tracking bond-wire and die-attach/solder-related degradation. It also discusses gate-related degradation observed during the test. This is the corpus's key primary source linking package-interconnect and thermal observations to power-cycling stress, and it reports multi-parameter evidence rather than single-observable diagnoses.

documents.title: Review of Prognosis Approaches Applied to Power SiC MOSFETs for Health State and Remaining Useful Life Prediction
documents.citation: S. Kumar, B. Allard, M. Hologne-Carpentier, G. Clerc and F. Auger, "Review of Prognosis Approaches Applied to Power SiC MOSFETs for Health State and Remaining Useful Life Prediction," Entropy, vol. 28, no. 2, art. 234, 2026. doi:10.3390/e28020234
documents.description: Open-access review (Entropy 28(2):234, 33 pages). Surveys prognosis and health-state/remaining-useful-life estimation for power SiC MOSFETs: reviewed degradation indicators include on-state resistance, threshold voltage, gate leakage and on-state voltage, alongside package-level mechanisms such as bond-wire and die-attach/sinter degradation and thermal resistance, under power-cycling, thermal-cycling and bias-stress conditions. A central finding of the review is that indicator-to-mechanism relationships are ambiguous and require multi-parameter, model-based reasoning - directly supporting this corpus's no-one-to-one-mapping rule.

documents.title: On the effect of SiC power MOSFET gate oxide degradation in high frequency phase leg-based applications
documents.organization: University of Sheffield / White Rose Research Online
documents.publisher: IEEE (ECCE 2022) - accepted-version copy at White Rose Research Online
documents.citation: J. Naghibi, S. Mohsenzade, S. Iqbal et al., "On the effect of SiC power MOSFET gate oxide degradation in high frequency phase leg-based applications," in IEEE Energy Conversion Congress and Expo (ECCE 2022), Detroit, Michigan, USA, 9-13 Oct 2022. Accepted version, White Rose Research Online, eprint 192716.
documents.description: Open-access primary research added to fill the gate-oxide coverage gap left by paywalled candidates P1-P8 (7 pages, accepted-version copy). Examines gate-oxide degradation in SiC power MOSFETs in high-frequency phase-leg applications, using threshold-voltage and gate-leakage behaviour as monitored quantities under gate stress. Its framing explicitly separates package-level failure modes (wire bond, solder layer) from chip-level gate-oxide effects, and treats gate-oxide degradation as progressive rather than as an instantaneous event.

documents.title: Precursors of Gate Oxide Degradation in Silicon Carbide MOSFETs
documents.citation: U. Karki and F. Z. Peng, "Precursors of Gate Oxide Degradation in Silicon Carbide MOSFETs," arXiv:1802.08085, 2018.
documents.description: Open-access primary research (6 pages, arXiv preprint, Michigan State University) added to fill the gate-oxide precursor gap. Demonstrates that threshold voltage, gate plateau voltage and gate plateau time respond to gate-oxide degradation in SiC MOSFETs, and explains why gate-oxide stress is more consequential in SiC than in Si. It is a precursor-identification study, i.e. it identifies candidate indicators that require corroboration; it is a preprint and is flagged as such.

documents.title: SiC Power MOSFET Gate Oxide Breakdown Reliability - Current Status
documents.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
documents.citation: K. P. Cheung, "SiC Power MOSFET Gate Oxide Breakdown Reliability - Current Status," Engineering Physics Division, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).
documents.description: Open-access government-laboratory publication (5 pages, NIST) added to fill the gate-oxide reliability gap. Reviews the current status of SiC power MOSFET gate-oxide breakdown reliability, including intrinsic versus extrinsic failure, time-dependent dielectric breakdown behaviour, the role of oxide thickness and field, and how operating-life screening relates to field reliability. It explicitly argues against simplistic reliability extrapolation, which supports the corpus's uncertainty-preserving stance. No publication year or venue is printed in the retrieved PDF, so publication_year is left null rather than inferred.
